title: Uncertainty and failure analysis
outcome: By the end, I can explain uncertainty and failure analysis using a traced example and a stated limitation.
scenario: Keep positive-class probability separate from confidence in the chosen label.
given: Supplied p(class 1): A: 0.9 reference 0; B: 0.6 reference 1; C: 0.2 reference 0. Predict class 1 at p>=0.5; confidence=max(p, 1-p).
All inputs and outcomes in this worked example are invented classroom data; no real model run is claimed.

steps.label: Predictions
steps.detail: A predicts 1 wrong; B predicts 1 correct; C predicts 0 correct.

steps.label: Selected-label confidence
steps.detail: Confidences are 0.9, 0.6, 0.8. C’s confidence is 0.8 despite p(class 1)=0.2.

steps.label: Selective review
steps.detail: Accept confidence>=0.8: A and C; accuracy 1/2 and coverage 2/3.

explanation: Positive-class probability and confidence in the chosen label differ when the predicted class is zero. For C, a class-one probability of 0.2 gives class-zero confidence 0.8 under this toy rule. Selective accuracy counts only accepted cases; coverage counts how many were accepted. A stricter cutoff can retain a confidently wrong case and lower accuracy on this supplied set.

counterfactual.prediction: Only A is accepted: accuracy 0/1, coverage 1/3.
counterfactual.reason: The most confident supplied case is wrong; a stricter cutoff is not guaranteed to improve this set’s accuracy.

student_task: What is C’s positive-class probability and chosen-label confidence? Point to the relevant step in the picture, then write the changed result and the rule or evidence that supports it.
teacher_answer: p(class 1)=0.2; predicted class 0 has selected-label confidence 0.8. These quantities answer different questions. Changed-case check: Only A is accepted: accuracy 0/1, coverage 1/3. The most confident supplied case is wrong; a stricter cutoff is not guaranteed to improve this set’s accuracy.
project_evidence: For your Image-pattern Network Investigation, save the input, procedure, observed result and limitation of this check. Label this worked example as practice; use a different, previously unreviewed case when checking independent understanding.
limits: Supplied scores are not proven calibrated. Review policies need representative held-out evidence and clear handling of rejected cases.
